chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: Allah does not cause an oppressor to be conquered except by an oppressor,
and this is His Word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And thus do We make some of the unjust to befriend others.'

key_terms.انْتَصَرَ: to be avenged / to be conquered
key_terms.بَعْضَ الظَّالِمِينَ بَعْضاً: some of the unjust to others
key_terms.نُوَلِّي: We make them rule / We assign authority

ai.seo_question: How does Allah defeat oppressors according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the divine principle of 'using the unjust to punish the unjust,' illustrating how Allah employs one tyrant as an instrument of retribution against another. This concept, rooted in Surah Al-An'am (6:129), reflects the Shia understanding of divine wisdom in history, where temporary dominance of the wicked serves as both a test for the faithful and a mechanism of cosmic justice. The hadith underscores that oppression often begets oppression, fulfilling the Quranic promise that the unjust will eventually face the consequences of their own actions through the agency of others.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not Cause an oppressor to be conquered except by an oppressor,
and these are the Words of the Mighty and Majestic [6:129] And thus do We make some of the unjust to befriend others’.
en.sarwar: 19. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from Ali ibn abu Hamza from abu Basir from his father abu la’ far (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Allah retaliates an oppressor through another oppressor only.
It is in the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘Thus do We make the unjust friends of one another because of their evil deeds.’” [6:129]
